subject: Itemfit: Rows in supplied and starting value data.frame objects do not match

messages.author: 051f9e22cdcba7f5
messages.subject: Itemfit: Rows in supplied and starting value data.frame objects do not match
parts:
Dear Dr. Chalmers,

once again I approached a problem, perhaps resulting again from the number of missings I have in my data set, I hope you will find time to suggest a solution.

I am fitting a graded response model:

data_tasks = read.csv("d2.csv", header = TRUE, dec=".", sep = ";", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
grm <- mirt(data_tasks, model=1, itemtype="graded", technical = list(removeEmptyRows=TRUE))

After executing itemfit I receive the following error:

itemfit(grm, fit_stats = "X2*_df")

Item re-scored so that all values are within a distance of 1
Error: Rows in supplied and starting value data.frame objects do not match. Were the
             data or itemtype input arguments modified?


Could you please suggest, what could cause the problem and how to solve it? Any help from you will be appreciated.

Best regards
Maciek

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Itemfit: Rows in supplied and starting value data.frame objects do not match
parts:
Hi Maciek,

Thanks for the report, this looks to be a bug related to the pattern of missing data causing issues in the parametric bootstrap scheme. The fix was to simply re-draw the dataset within each iteration to ensure that at least 1 unique value of the respective categories are observed for each item. The fix is on the development version on Github.

Phil

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Itemfit: Rows in supplied and starting value data.frame objects do not match
parts:
Hi Maciek,

This largely has to do with the fact that your sample size is quite small (less than N=111 after removing empty rows) and the items have several options (some as high as 9 unique observations; use apply(data_tasks, 2, table)). This makes the data counts very sparse, which is what caused the problem you reported last time. It might be a better strategy to collapse categories that are sparse (if theoretically  justifiable), or otherwise abandon these itemfit statistics since they will be very under-powered anyway. 

Regarding the parametric bootstrap, because many of your cell counts were 1-2 in a good number of items the IRT intercept parameters are fairly extreme, so generating data where these observations are realized in a new random sample is unlikely. Hence, the data fails to create a reasonably close new sample with the same pattern of missingness 100x in a row. I think the scenario is just too extreme to work with here for these simulation fit statistics. You might have better luck when using alternatives? It's difficult to tell, but either way detecting misfit is going to be quite difficult given the effective sample size.

Phil
